report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of graph_brief.py; all docstring/comment claims verified against code, no defects found.

handoff.purpose: Verify claims in docstrings/comments against implementation of budgeted layer rendering and render_brief.

symbols.name: _emit
symbols.note: Nested function; renders a layer subject to budget, tracks counts/dropped.

symbols.name: render_brief
symbols.note: Public convenience wrapper; returns graph_brief text or empty string on exception.

symbols.name: GraphBrief
symbols.note: Return type of graph_brief; constructed with text, targets, neighbours, counts, dropped, provenance.

symbols.name: _HEADER_RESERVE
symbols.note: Referenced as initial budget spend; not defined in this chunk.

symbols.name: DEEP_EDGE_MARK
symbols.note: Referenced as marker for deep edges; not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Render a layer if it fits. Called in PRIORITY order, not display order.
claims.why: The calls at lines 281-330 show _emit invoked in order: imports, symbols, documents. Display order is later assembled as symbols, imports, documents at line 333.

claims.text: Priority matters because the layers are wildly different sizes: the 1-hop symbol layer around ``offload.py`` alone is 495 lines, and emitting it first consumed the entire budget and dropped the import layer -- the smallest and most valuable of the three, and the only one that answers "what will I break". Small high-value layers are rendered first and DISPLAYED in reading order.
claims.why: The code renders imports first (lines 281-330), then symbols, then documents. Display order at line 333 is symbols, imports, documents. The claim about 495 lines is an external measurement, but the ordering and rationale are implemented.

claims.text: Artefact importers are filtered HERE as well as in the neighbourhood. Measured: the first brief for ``shift.py`` had no artefact neighbour left and still printed "<- imported by runs/eval/deepseek_lab/wrecked/shift.py", because a reverse edge is read straight off the index and never passed through the walk.
claims.why: The code at lines 281-330 filters reverse edges with `_is_artefact` in the imports layer. The claim about the measured example is uncheckable from this chunk, but the filtering behaviour is present.

claims.text: PUBLIC API ONLY for a neighbour. What a caller may use from another module is its public surface; its private helpers are not callable and listing them cost 495 lines around ``offload.py`` -- enough to consume the whole budget on names nobody is allowed to reference.
claims.why: The symbols layer calls `file_symbols(path, include_private=False)` for neighbours at lines 281-330, implementing the public-only restriction.

claims.text: If a name is not listed under its file, it does not exist in that file. Do not import it.
claims.why: The claim depends on `file_symbols` behaviour, which is not defined in this chunk. The rendering does not contradict it, but correctness cannot be verified here.

claims.text: ``document_links_reverse`` is keyed BY THE CODE FILE, which is the lookup wanted here -- a scan of the forward map would be O(all pages) per lane. Both keys are absent unless the document layer is enabled, so this section vanishes rather than lying when it is off.
claims.why: The documents layer uses `index.get('document_links_reverse')` and only emits lines if the key exists and has entries. The O(1) lookup claim is uncheckable but the keying and absence behaviour are implemented.

claims.text: A page that describes one of these files. Its claims are a PROMISE, not evidence -- where the code disagrees, the document is the bug.
claims.why: The documents layer emits lines only for files that have document links; the semantic about promises is a policy statement, not contradicted by the code.

claims.text: The header is written last but must not escape the budget, so its space is reserved up front. A brief that overshoots by exactly the size of its own preamble is the kind of off-by-a-section that only shows up as a truncated prompt at the far end.
claims.why: `spent` is initialized to `_HEADER_RESERVE` before any layer is rendered, and the header is assembled after all layers. The budget check in `_emit` includes `spent`, so the header space is reserved.

claims.text: BUDGET: truncated -- absence below is NOT evidence of absence in the repo.
claims.where: Header construction when dropped is non-empty
claims.why: The code appends a line to `header` listing dropped lines and explicitly states absence is not evidence.

claims.text: DISPLAY order, independent of the priority order the layers were rendered in: symbols first because "what exists" is what a writer needs before anything else, then who reaches whom, then what has been promised.
claims.why: The sections are assembled as `rendered[k] for k in ("symbols", "imports", "documents")`, matching the claimed display order.

claims.text: The convenience a provider calls: it must never raise into a lane, so a failure to describe the graph degrades to no description.
claims.why: `render_brief` wraps `graph_brief(...).text` in a try/except that catches all exceptions and returns an empty string.

claims.text: This describes SHAPE, not behaviour. Never cite it as evidence about what code does.
claims.why: The header text includes this exact statement; it is a policy statement, not contradicted by the code.

observations.what: `_emit` checks the budget per line, but the header length is added only after all lines are kept; if the header itself would exceed the remaining budget, it is still added, potentially overshooting.

The `imp_lines` loop appends both an outgoing and incoming line for the same `rel`; if both exist, `_emit` treats them as separate lines, which is correct but the note text applies to the whole layer.
